conviction_note: Findings net to about zero (+0.2): the September-quarter collapse in smartphone (-22%) and PC (-20 to -22%) units and a new CEO's first FY guide point to a soft FY27/Q1 guide, but TV units (Dolby's largest device market) were +1%, Q4 is largely contracted via the Meta VDP deal against a consensus already below the guide midpoint, and short interest has built to 10 days to cover, which cushions a merely in-line guide. abs_move 8.0 (implied 7.2 with a 43%-of-mid ATM spread, history median 7.0, first FY27 guide under a new CEO adds); p_up 47 leans with the 5.4-point put skew only slightly, so the scaled number (-0.5) and the finding sum (+0.2) disagree in sign by a rounding margin, both meaning 'no edge on direction'.
bar: Q4 FY26 revenue consensus $368.4M and non-GAAP EPS $1.19 (Earnings Whispers preview 2026-11-10, https://finviz.com/news/420638/dolbys-meta-video-deal-faces-its-first-real-test-as-fiscal-year-closes); Benzinga $371.9M / $1.14 (via search snippet of https://www.benzinga.com/quote/DLB/earnings, page 403 on fetch). Company guide (8-K ex.99.1 2026-07-30, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001308547/000119312526326149/d165402dex991.htm): Q4 revenue $362-392M, licensing $335-365M, non-GAAP EPS $1.13-1.28; FY26 $1.41-1.44B, non-GAAP EPS $4.25-4.40. Consensus sits in the lower half of the guide. FY27 bar weakly sourced: MarketScreener FY27 net sales ~$1,467M (https://ca.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/DOLBY-LABORATORIES-INC-12317/finances/, snippet), FY27 EPS ~$4.63 from a stale March snapshot; Q1 FY27 EPS ~$1.06 (Benzinga snippet) vs Q1 FY26 actual $1.06 incl. a $7M true-up. The stock trades on the next-quarter/FY guide, for which the bar is single-sourced, so guidance findings are capped small.
positioning_check: Short interest 6,006,027 shares at the 2026-10-30 settlement, 10.01 days to cover on 600k avg volume, ~6.4% of 93.67M shares outstanding (higher as a share of the Class A float); up from 5.53M on 2026-09-15 and 3.48M on 2026-03-13 (https://equibles.com/stocks/dlb/shortinterest, fetched 2026-11-17). Shorts have been building into the print. Baseline: 25d skew +5.42 vol points (downside paid), put/call OI 0.87, total OI only 1,220 contracts, ATM spread 43% of mid so the 7.23% event-implied move is indicative. Tape: -6.21% over 5 days, -2.66% over 20 days, -12.2% from 52w high. Earnings Whispers reports bearish sentiment readings rising to 55.7% from 37.8% before the last print (finviz preview 2026-11-10).

findings.finding: The Q4 (Jul-Sep) quarter is largely contracted: CFO Robert Park said Meta signed 'a large deal' with the Video Distribution Program early in Q4 and that mobile minimum volume commitments are back-end loaded into Q4, both inside the $362-392M guide given 2026-07-30; consensus ($368-372M revenue, $1.14-1.21 EPS) sits $5-9M below the $377M midpoint, so a revenue print near or above the midpoint is a ~1-2% beat of consensus.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Jan 2026 (Q1 FY26) revenue $347M beat with a $7M true-up and a raised FY guide: +1.84%. Jul 2026 Q3 was within guide but the Q4 guide with the Meta deal drove +13.58%; Apr 2026 -10.41% was on a Q3 guide far below consensus. Reported-quarter beats have been paid little; the guide decides.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus sitting below the guide midpoint although the largest swing item (Meta) was already signed when the guide was set shows the street haircut Q4 for the memory shock; if the contracted nature were priced, consensus would sit at or above the midpoint. Small because it lands inside what the company already guided.
findings.independence: Bar from Earnings Whispers preview https://finviz.com/news/420638/dolbys-meta-video-deal-faces-its-first-real-test-as-fiscal-year-closes (2026-11-10). Shares the transcript with the Meta-comp finding below (different line: FY27 comp).

findings.finding: Dolby's fiscal Q4 shipment quarter (CQ3 2026) saw global smartphone units fall 22.0% YoY to 255.3M (IDC, 2026-10-14; Xiaomi -29%, OPPO -35%, vivo -32%, Samsung -6%, Apple -4%) and PC units fall 20-22% (IDC -20.1%, Gartner -22.4%, Omdia -21.2% with a further -24% forecast for CQ4), against IDC's -6.7% for CQ2 that was the latest datapoint when Dolby guided on 2026-07-30 with FY26 mobile 'up mid single digits'; IDC says 'the worst is yet to come' and sees 2027 down again, while Park had said that 'the longer this goes on... it starts to flow through' — pressure on the Q1 FY27 and FY27 guide and on true-ups.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guide-driven: Apr 2026 Q3 guide $295-325M vs $343M consensus -10.41%; Nov 2025 first FY26 guide below estimates (Reuters 'Dolby down after holiday-quarter forecast misses estimates') closed +0.06% after an intraday drop.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the stock is -12% from its high, -6.2% in five days, short interest rose 0.5M shares since mid-Sept and puts are bid. What is not visibly priced is the size of the step-down: consensus still carries FY27 revenue ~+3% (~$1.47B) and Q1 FY27 EPS flat YoY at ~$1.06, which would be visibly lower if analysts had marked mobile/PC royalties to a 20%+ unit decline. Net of the rest: TV (largest device market) was +1% in CQ3, broadcast and auto/VDP ('Other', guided up high teens) are growing, MVCs delay the hit, and Dolby's premium-tier mix (Apple/Samsung only -4/-6%) dampens it, so mobile+PC (roughly a quarter of licensing) at -20% units is a few percent of licensing, not more.
findings.independence: PC series: Gartner https://www.gartner.com/en/newsroom/press-releases/2026-10-12-gartner-says-worldwide-pc-shipments-declined-22-point-4-percent-in-third-quarter-of-2026-as-component-cost-inflation-raised-asps (2026-10-12); counterparty: Qualcomm handset revenue -26% in its Sept quarter (https://zacks.com/stock/news/3024519/qcom-q4-earnings-beat-estimates-on-robust-automotive-growth). Proxy: industry units, not Dolby's own royalty report.

findings.finding: Qualcomm (2026-11-04), the handset counterparty that reported after Dolby last spoke, said QCT handset sales to Chinese OEMs bottomed in the September quarter and are expected to return to double-digit sequential growth in the December quarter, while raising chip prices to pass through memory costs — a datapoint against a further leg down in Dolby's Q1 FY27 (Oct-Dec) mobile units.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No company-specific history on a counterparty bottoming call; Dolby's guide line has moved the stock 10-14% on the two most recent prints.
findings.why_not_priced: DLB has fallen 6% since Qualcomm's call, so the market is weighting the -26% handset headline and Qualcomm's below-consensus EPS guide, not the China-bottoming comment; if the bottoming were priced, the five-day tape and the put skew would not lean down into a guide.
findings.independence: Same Qualcomm print is cited for the -26% in the units finding; this finding uses only its forward bottoming statement. IDC notes memory inflation slowed to low double digits q/q in CQ3 (https://www.idc.com/resource-center/press-releases/smartphone-shipments-decline-3q26/), which also points to stabilisation, though IDC itself says the market has not bottomed.

findings.finding: This is the first earnings call and first FY guide under CEO Marc Whitten (effective 2026-08-27, ex-Meta robotics/Xbox/Sonos), and on 2026-11-09/10 the compensation committee adopted a fiscal-2027 executive bonus plan paid on non-GAAP operating income and revenue (CEO at 100% of target) plus a new standardized executive severance policy with a change-in-control tier (8-K filed 2026-11-13) — a setup in which a new CEO has an incentive to set an achievable FY27 guide and may announce reorganisation.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior Dolby CEO transition in the 7-print baseline; the first FY guide in Nov 2025 under the old CEO missed estimates and closed +0.06%.
findings.why_not_priced: The 8-K landed four days before the print as a routine compensation filing and was not covered by the previews; consensus FY27 numbers (~+3% revenue, EPS ~$4.6, partly stale) do not look like they assume a rebase. It is an inference about behaviour, not a document stating the guide, so it is small.
findings.independence: CEO appointment 8-K https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001308547/000119312526369707/d349287d8k.htm (2026-08-27) and https://audioxpress.com/news/dolby-laboratories-announces-leadership-transition-with-marc-whitten-as-new-president-ceo-and-director. No source states what the guide will be.

findings.finding: Short interest built to 6.01M shares (10.0 days to cover, ~6.4% of shares outstanding and a larger share of the Class A float) at the 2026-10-30 settlement, up from 5.53M in mid-September and 3.48M in March, so the memory/handset bear case is positioned and an in-line FY27 guide could force covering.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Jul 2026: a guide that beat a bearish setup moved the stock +13.58%, the largest reaction in the 7-print history.
findings.why_not_priced: Short interest is the positioning, not a priced fact; 10 days to cover on a name with 0.6-0.8M shares a day means the squeeze mechanism exists if the guide is merely in line. It would be visibly priced if short interest had fallen into the print; it rose.
findings.independence: Earnings Whispers bearish sentiment rose to 55.7% from 37.8% (https://finviz.com/news/420638/dolbys-meta-video-deal-faces-its-first-real-test-as-fiscal-year-closes); baseline 25d skew +5.42 (downside paid).

findings.finding: TV, Dolby's largest device end market and the one management called among the 'lesser impacted' by memory, shipped +1% YoY in CQ3 2026 per Counterpoint's monthly tracker, against -20%+ for phones and PCs.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No TV-specific reaction history; the stock moves on the total guide.
findings.source_date: 2026-10 (Counterpoint monthly tracker, per search summary; exact page date not verified)
findings.why_not_priced: The memory narrative is told in phone and PC units; a flat TV quarter limits how far the device-licensing total can fall, which the 5-day selloff into the print does not reflect.
findings.independence: Fool transcript (2026-08-03) quotes Park calling TV the 'largest device market' and among the least memory-affected. Proxy, not Dolby's royalty number; source date only snippet-level.

findings.finding: Auto, Dolby's fastest-growing end market (inside 'Other', guided up high teens for FY26 with VDP), had strong counterparty data in the September quarter: Qualcomm automotive revenue +89% to ~$1.99B and InterDigital's CE/IoT/auto licensing +97% to $56M while its smartphone licensing fell 10%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Management said it may break out auto from FY27; no reaction history on the line.
findings.why_not_priced: The growth lines that offset mobile/PC in an FY27 guide are not in any preview; the previews discuss only memory and Meta. Small: auto is still a minority of licensing and these are proxies.
findings.independence: Qualcomm auto +89% https://zacks.com/stock/news/3024519/qcom-q4-earnings-beat-estimates-on-robust-automotive-growth (shared with the Qualcomm findings, different line).

findings.finding: Adeia, a media-IP licensing peer, cut its FY26 revenue outlook by ~$20M on 2026-11-02 after Q3 revenue fell 8.2% YoY to $80.2M, citing shifting execution timelines of several large license agreements — a reminder that licensing deal timing slips into the next year.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Dolby's Q3 FY26 was itself 'offset by deal timing'; that print still rose +13.58% on the Q4 guide.
findings.why_not_priced: Weak peer read; the $20M cut is from a secondary summary and the mechanism (Adeia's own deal timing) has no link to Dolby's licensees, so it is sized near zero.

findings.finding: The Q4 23% YoY revenue growth guided for is flattered by the initial Meta VDP agreement and back-end-loaded MVCs; management did not say whether Meta includes prior-period royalties, and the Nov-10 preview calls it 'not a guaranteed recurring source', so Q1 FY27 will step down sequentially from Q4 and FY27 growth faces a harder comp.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 guide in Nov 2025 below estimates: stock fell intraday and closed +0.06%.
findings.why_not_priced: Q1 FY27 EPS consensus (~$1.06) is already below Q4 consensus ($1.19), so a sequential step-down is partly expected; what is not known is whether Meta was a catch-up. Small.
findings.independence: Fool transcript 2026-08-03 (same call as the reported-quarter finding): Park said Q3 true-ups were 'less than a million', no statement on Meta catch-up.

findings.finding: Dolby raised its buyback authorization by $350M to ~$427M in Q3 FY26, repurchased 1.2M shares for $65M in that quarter and said repurchases have been 'stepping up year to date'; at ~$60.7 the stock is near the lower end of its year.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No reaction history on buyback announcements in the baseline.
findings.why_not_priced: Known since July; the only new piece is the Q4 repurchase amount disclosed tonight. Small.
